newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stock market gets freer rein, seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Manila stock market gets freer rein, seen growing.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) won self-regulatory powers on Monday in a move government and bourse officials said would attract more funds into the market.

The bourse was given self-regulating organisation (SRO) status by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) after it underwent a series of reforms to ensure transparent stock trading and adequate safeguards to prevent insider trading.

"Investors will see that the granting of this status as bestowing confidence on the Philippine Stock Exchange itself... Seeing that we are self-regulating, it means that we know what we are doing, that we are mature and we are capable," PSE chairman Wilson Sy told reporters.
Sy said such confidence would bring higher trading volumes because the exchange would be professionally run.

"This puts us in the same league as the U.S. stock exchanges and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It should translate into a more efficient and more transparent stock market," said Roman Azanza, chairman of the Capital Market Development Council.
The Philippine bourse has been growing rapidly in the past few years. By mid- 1996, the market was capitalised at $64 billion, up from $5.757 billion in 1990.

Foreign brokerage houses have been setting up local operations in the country and the price of an exchange seat is now about 90 million pesos ($3.4 million), up from four million ($152,090) to five million pesos ($190,114) in 1993.

Under SRO status, the PSE has the authority to audit and sanction its more than 200 member-brokers. It will also allow the bourse to streamline initial public offerings procedures and ensure their wide distribution.
For its part, the exchange has instituted several reforms including the establishment of a central depository organisation and a clearing house to ease trading.
"This is a step in the right direction as we go forward towards more quality trading... The benefit of scripless trading is in the volume," PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas said.
President Fidel Ramos, who witnessed the ceremony, said the bestowing of the status is part of his government's measures to liberalise the securities industry.

"Far too many ventures have been frustrated; far too many entrepreneurial dreams have been dashed to pieces; and far too many good ideas have died before birth -- because some government agencies in the past have suffocated them with restrictive policies," Ramos said.
However, SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said the regulatory authority would still have an oversight function over the PSE.
Yasay said the watchdog agency would still recommend changes in trading rules if it deemed them necessary, adding that any change in the present rules would also need the SEC's approval.
He also said the SEC could fine for any wrongdoing or even suspend the licence of the exchange. ($1 = 26.3 pesos)
